chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, altogether from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Anbasa, from Abu Abdillah (AS) who said:
'Drink from the residue (su'r) of the menstruating woman, but do not perform wudu from it.'

key_terms.الْحَائِض: al-ha'id — a woman in the state of menstruation (hayd); her ritual status affects various rulings in Islamic law
key_terms.تَوَضَّأ: wudu — the minor ritual ablution required before salat and certain other acts of worship
key_terms.سُؤْر: su'r — the leftover water or food remaining after a person or animal has drunk or eaten from it; a key legal category in Islamic ritual law

ai.seo_question: Can you drink the leftover water of a menstruating woman? Can her su'r be used for wudu?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) rules that while the residual drinking water (su'r) of a menstruating woman is permissible to consume, it may not be used for performing wudu (ritual ablution). This ruling reflects the classical Shia jurisprudential principle that ritual purity requirements for worship differ from general food purity — drinking water from a shared vessel is permissible, but the same water does not suffice for the ritual purity needed for salat.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, altogether from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Mansour Bin Hazim, from Anbasat, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Drink from the residue of the menstruating woman but do not perform Ablution (Wudhu) from it’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn and Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan all from Safwan ibn Yahya from Mansur ibn Hazim from ‘Anbasah who has said the following: “Abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that it is permissible for you to drink the leftover water from which a woman during her Hayd (menses) has drunk but do not take Wudu 5 with it.”
